name: Great Replacement conspiracy theory
summary: The Great Replacement is the claim, coined by Renaud Camus, that the native French and white European peoples are being replaced by non-white, mostly African and Muslim, peoples through mass immigration that 'replacist' elites want and promote. It treats this as the central question of politics, asks for the migrants' return (remigration), and values ethnically and culturally homogeneous nations. Its own text says little on the economy, institutions or most social questions.
scope: Represents the theory as Camus states it (Le Grand Remplacement 2011, as restated in You Will Not Replace Us!, 2018) and as ISD, ADL, SPLC and Coates describe it. Excludes the broader white genocide conspiracy theory (its own Wikipedia article), identitarian organisations, politicians and media hosts who repeat it, and the killers who cited it: none of their platforms is evidence here. Critics' accounts (ISD, ADL, SPLC) serve as the gate and as definitions; answers rest on Camus's own text.
